Loading packages, Dust2 snapshots and filtering out round start snapshots, and from that keeping only match_id, tick, name, side, x, y, z, round_num, team_clan_name, health.

```{r}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, stringr)
setwd("/home/augustas/Documents/DM/Data Mining/Project/CSGO/Github/cs2-rop-main/data/processed")

snapshot_files = list.files(path = "/home/augustas/Documents/DM/Data Mining/Project/CSGO/Github/cs2-rop-main/data/processed", pattern = "snapshots.parquet", recursive = TRUE)

snapshot_data = data.frame()

for (file in snapshot_files){
  path = paste("/home/augustas/Documents/DM/Data Mining/Project/CSGO/Github/cs2-rop-main/data/processed/", file, sep="")
  current_file = as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(path))
  if( str_detect(current_file$match_id[1], "dust2") ){
    next
  }
  
  # Getting the round start snapshots.
  round_start_snapshots = current_file %>%
    distinct(tick, round_num) %>%
    arrange(tick) %>%
    group_by(round_num) %>%
    mutate(
      snapshot_number = row_number(),
      remove_snapshot = snapshot_number == 1
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Removing the round start snapshots. The logic is that
  # in the first snapshot, the players are not moving.
  # This creates high density cells at the spawns,
  # which is not very informative for round outcome prediction
  current_file = current_file %>%
    anti_join(
      round_start_snapshots %>%
        filter(remove_snapshot) %>%
        select(tick),
      by = "tick"
    )
  
  snapshot_data = bind_rows(current_file, snapshot_data)
}

snapshot_data_filtered = snapshot_data %>%
  select(match_id, tick, name, side, x, y, z, round_num, team_clan_name, health) %>%
  mutate(dead = ifelse(health > 0, F, T)) %>% # Adding a player dead field
  select(!health)

rm(snapshot_data)
```

Quadtree code from player coordinates throughout all matches.

```{r}
map_min_x = min(snapshot_data_filtered$x)
map_max_x = max(snapshot_data_filtered$x)

map_min_y = min(snapshot_data_filtered$y)
map_max_y = max(snapshot_data_filtered$y)

players = snapshot_data_filtered %>%
  select(x, y, dead) %>%
  filter(dead == T) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# --- VIBE CODING THE QUADTREE WITH CHATGPT STARTS HERE ---

count_points = function(cell, players){
  # If player coordinates fall into cell coordinates
  # Add that player to the player count for that cell
  sum(
    players$x >= cell$xmin &
      players$x < cell$xmax &
      players$y >= cell$ymin &
      players$y < cell$ymax
  )
}

subdivide_cell = function(cell, players, threshold, max_depth){
  # Get how many players are in current cell
  count = count_points(cell, players)
  
  # If the number of players in current cell is less or eq to the threshold OR
  # If the depth of division of the current cell is larger or equal to the max
  # Return the undivided cell
  if(count <= threshold || cell$depth >= max_depth){
    cell$count = count
    return(list(cell))
  }
  
  # Get current cell coordinate midpoints
  xmid = (cell$xmin + cell$xmax) / 2 
  ymid = (cell$ymin + cell$ymax) / 2
  
  # Subdivided cell coordinates
  children = data.frame(
    # View the children cells as:
    # _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
    #       |
    # Cell 1| Cell 2
    # _ _ _ | _ _ _ _
    #       |
    # Cell 3| Cell 4
    # _ _ _ | _ _ _ _
    #
    # So in left-to-right order:
    # xmin_cell1 = xmin, xmin_cell2 = xmid, xmin_cell3 = xmin ...
    # xmax_cell1 = xmid, xmax_cell2 = xmax ...
    # And so on. The cells share some of the points
    # Which is why they are laid out like so
    xmin = c(cell$xmin, xmid, cell$xmin, xmid),
    xmax = c(xmid, cell$xmax, xmid, cell$xmax),
    ymin = c(cell$ymin, cell$ymin, ymid, ymid),
    ymax = c(ymid, ymid, cell$ymax, cell$ymax),
    depth = cell$depth + 1
  )
  result = list()
  
  # Recursive subdivision into four smaller cells
  for(i in 1:4){
    result = c(
      result,
      subdivide_cell(
        children[i, ],
        players,
        threshold,
        max_depth
      )
    )
  }
  result
}

# Start with initial cell which is the entire map with no subdivisions
initial_cell = data.frame(
  xmin = map_min_x,
  xmax = map_max_x,
  ymin = map_min_y,
  ymax = map_max_y,
  depth = 0
)

# VIBE CODING THE QUADTREE WITH CHATGPT ENDS HERE
```

Creating the adaptive grids for different cell player count thresholds

```{r}
# Create the adaptive grid by binding the recursive subdivisions
# Single map testing showed 100 and 80 to be a good player num threshold, so
# the assumption is that threshold*map_number should be good too

# The cells are not normalized according to count / area, so they 
# Represent direct counts, not densities (frequency of cell occupancy).
# Adding density field which is normalized compared to the player counts
adaptive_grid_t60 = do.call(
  rbind,
  subdivide_cell(
    initial_cell,
    players,
    threshold = 60*length(unique(snapshot_data_filtered$match_id)),
    max_depth = 7
  )
)%>%
  mutate(area = (xmax-xmin) * (ymax-ymin)) %>%
  mutate(density = count / area)

adaptive_grid_t80 = do.call(
  rbind,
  subdivide_cell(
    initial_cell,
    players,
    threshold = 80*length(unique(snapshot_data_filtered$match_id)),
    max_depth = 7
  )
)%>%
  mutate(area = (xmax-xmin) * (ymax-ymin)) %>%
  mutate(density = count / area)

adaptive_grid_t100 = do.call(
  rbind,
  subdivide_cell(
    initial_cell,
    players,
    threshold = 100*length(unique(snapshot_data_filtered$match_id)),
    max_depth = 7
  )
)%>%
  mutate(area = (xmax-xmin) * (ymax-ymin)) %>%
  mutate(density = count / area)

adaptive_grid_t120 = do.call(
  rbind,
  subdivide_cell(
    initial_cell,
    players,
    threshold = 120*length(unique(snapshot_data_filtered$match_id)),
    max_depth = 7
  )
)%>%
  mutate(area = (xmax-xmin) * (ymax-ymin)) %>%
  mutate(density = count / area)
```

Plotting all that shit

```{r}
thr_60 = ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = adaptive_grid_t60,
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = ymin,
      ymax = ymax,
      fill = density
    ),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    limits = c(
      0,
      quantile(adaptive_grid_t60$density, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    oob = scales::squish
  ) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal()

thr_60
```
